en: The *Vajraśekhara-yoga-akṣasūtra*, excerpted from the one hundred thousand verses of the extensive commentary.
Compiled by the Grand Officer of the Household, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Duke of Sui with a fief of three thousand households, recipient of the purple robe, posthumously titled Minister of Works and conferred the posthumous name Dajian (Great Mirror).

Authored by the Tripitaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra of the Great Xingshan Temple, Possessor of Great and Vast Wisdom; translated by imperial decree. At that time, the World-Honored One Vairocana addressed Vajrapāṇi, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!"
For the sake of those bodhisattvas who practice the conduct of mantra and vidyā, he explains the various ritual procedures;
out of compassion for all sentient beings of the future, he explains the merits and benefits of the rosary.
"By hearing such a sublime intention, one will swiftly realize siddhi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrasattva addressed the Buddha, saying:
"So be it, World-Honored One!"
"I shall now explain it for you.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrasattva spoke these verses:
"The jewel symbolizes the supreme fruit of the Bodhisattva; Its being severed in the middle represents the cutting off of outflows (āsrava).”
The cord threading the beads represents Avalokiteśvara; The mother bead represents Amitāyus.
Be careful not to let it pass over [the head], lest you incur the offense of transgressing the Dharma; All merit is accumulated through the use of the prayer beads.
A rosary made of carnelian brings one-fold merit;
a rosary made of wood from the *kṣauma* tree brings two-fold merit;
and a rosary made of iron brings three-fold merit.
A rosary made of refined copper brings fourfold merit;
those made of crystal, pearl, and various jewels bring a hundredfold merit;
and one made of *vajra* brings a thousandfold merit, O Son of Śakra.
A rosary of *vajra* seeds brings ten million merits;
a rosary of lotus seeds brings a thousand times ten million merits;
a rosary of *bodhi* seeds brings immeasurable merits.
For the Buddha Family, one performs recitation with bodhi seeds;
for the Vajra Family, the rite is performed with vajra seeds;
and for the Ratna Family, one uses various jewels for recitation.
For the Lotus Family, use lotus seeds as beads;
for the Karma Family, they serve as a rosary, with various beads interspersed and strung together.
There are four distinct types of rosaries: the superior, the most excellent, the middling, and the inferior.
One thousand and eighty beads constitute the superior; one hundred and eight beads are the most excellent;
fifty-four beads constitute the middling; twenty-seven beads are of the inferior class.
Holding two rosaries at the heart, with a mind focused in meditative concentration free from discursive thought,
one-pointed in the yoga of the deity, one shall achieve all dharmas of both principle and phenomena.
Whether placed upon the topknot, worn upon the body, or set upon the neck or arms, whatever discourse is spoken becomes recitation; through this recitation, one purifies the three karmas.
By placing it upon the crown of the head, one purifies the immediate transgressions; by wearing it around the neck, one purifies the four grave offenses;
held in the hand or upon the arm, it removes all sins and enables the practitioner to quickly attain purification.
If one cultivates mantra-dhāraṇīs and recollects the names of the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas,
one shall obtain immeasurable and supreme merit, and all sought-after sublime vows will be fulfilled.
The method for consecrating and stringing the rosary is exactly as described in the Susiddhikara Sūtra.
One should understand that while the Yoga Tantra speaks only of its efficacy and underlying principles, it does not describe its physical characteristics.
The Vajraśekhara Yoga Akṣasūtra Sūtra (Vajraśekhara-yoga-akṣasūtra-sūtra)
